"""Requirement-driven application synthesis.

This package replaces the earlier ``replay`` package. Replay recognised an
incoming ``requirements.yaml`` by hashing it and unpacked a prebuilt archive;
it never read the specification. ``synth`` reads the specification, derives an
:class:`~synth.appspec.AppSpec` from it, and emits an application from a
capability library bound to that specification.

Public surface:

``synth.cli.run_synthesis``
    Entry point used by ``arc_main.py``.
``synth.appspec.AppSpec``
    The intermediate representation the emitter consumes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from synth.appspec import AppSpec
from synth.cli import run_synthesis
from synth.version import AGENT_BUILD, ARC_VERSION

__all__ = ["AppSpec", "AGENT_BUILD", "ARC_VERSION", "run_synthesis"]

"""The intermediate representation produced from a requirement set.

An :class:`AppSpec` is everything the emitter needs and nothing that is
specific to a library source file. It is JSON-serialisable so it can be written
next to the generated application as an auditable record of what was read out of
the specification.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

#: Domains the synthesiser can emit. ``generic`` is the fallback pack used when
#: a document describes nothing the capability library recognises.
DOMAINS = ("spreadsheet", "collab", "collab-stage1", "generic")


@dataclass(slots=True)
class RequirementRow:
    """One atomic requirement, flattened for the traceability report."""

    id: str
    name: str
    breadcrumb: str
    features: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    scenarios: int = 0
    named_controls: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    messages: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    artifacts: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self)


@dataclass(slots=True)
class AppSpec:
    """Everything the emitter binds into the capability library."""

    domain: str
    pack: str
    title: str
    source: str
    features: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    seed: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    catalog: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    substitutions: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    requirements: list[RequirementRow] = field(default_factory=list)
    diagnostics: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    app_type: str = "web"
    port: int = 3000

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        payload = asdict(self)
        payload["requirements"] = [row.to_dict() for row in self.requirements]
        return payload

    def to_json(self) -> str:
        return json.dumps(self.to_dict(), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=False)

    def write(self, path: Path) -> None:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(self.to_json() + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def summary_lines(self) -> list[str]:
        rows = [
            f"  domain          : {self.domain}",
            f"  capability pack : {self.pack}",
            f"  title           : {self.title}",
            f"  requirement set : {self.source}",
            f"  atomic reqs     : {len(self.requirements)}",
            f"  scenarios       : {sum(row.scenarios for row in self.requirements)}",
            f"  features        : {len(self.features)}",
            f"  catalog entries : {len(self.catalog)}",
        ]
        seed = self.seed or {}
        if "workbook" in seed:
            rows.append(f"  seeded workbook : {seed.get('workbook')!r} sheets={seed.get('sheets')}")
            rows.append(f"  seeded cells    : {len(seed.get('cells') or {})}")
            if seed.get("rejected_fixtures"):
                rows.append(f"  rejected fixtures: {len(seed['rejected_fixtures'])} (contradict an applied family)")
        for key in ("accounts", "organizations", "repositories", "issues", "pull_requests", "teams", "branches", "files"):
            values = seed.get(key)
            if values:
                rows.append(f"  seeded {key:<10}: {len(values)}")
        if self.warnings:
            rows.append(f"  warnings        : {len(self.warnings)} (see .arc/spec.json)")
        return rows

    *,
    node_id: str,
    requirement_data: dict[str, Any],
    dynamic_context: str,
    interface_contract: str = "",

    sections = []
    if test_intent.strip():
        operation = "Modify" if replace_test_id else "Generate"
        replacement_rules = (

            else "Do not replace unrelated current-node tests; return only tests that serve this requested intent."
        )
        sections.append(
            section(
                "Requested Test Intent",
                [
                    f"{operation} coverage specifically for this intent: {test_intent.strip()}",
                    replacement_rules,
                ],
            )
        )
    if interface_contract.strip():
        sections.append(f"### Current Interface Contract\n{interface_contract.strip()}")
    sections.append(
        section(
            "Task",
            [
                "Generate tests for the current node ownership. If no layer is appropriate for this node, return an empty `tests` list with a clear `summary`.",
                "This is a generation-only pass: create tests and the returned manifest, then stop. Do not run, reread, or self-repair files written in this pass; TestDrivenDeveloper receives all test repair work.",

                "Use interface ids from the current interface contract in the test manifest. Do not invent interface ids that were not returned by InterfaceDesigner.",
                "For leaf nodes, tests must drive the final desired behavior. Do not write tests that pass against placeholder skeletons, `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` responses, 501 responses, fake success messages, or intentionally unimplemented branches.",

                "If the scenario changes authentication state, tests should check that the shared app state reflects the transition, such as shared controls changing to current-user/account state, protected/public navigation updating, command access changing, or `/api/auth/session` returning the expected user/session after the action.",
                "If the scenario changes cart, checkout, account, product, order, catalog, or inventory state, tests should verify the visible result and the relevant API/service/persistence boundary when the current interface contract includes it.",
                "For E2E tests, choose selectors, prompts, command arguments, and observable outcomes from requirement-stated user-facing behavior first. If the requirement does not specify exact selectors or flags, define stable executable hooks in the test contract so implementation can align to them.",
                "For frontend tests containing JSX, the actual manifest `file_path` must end in `.test.tsx` or `.spec.tsx`; do not use a `.ts` bridge file that imports a `.tsx` test.",

                "Return `summary`, `tests`, and `files_written`.",
                "Each test manifest item must include `test_id`, `req_id`, `interface_ids`, `type`, `file_path`, and `first_line`.",
                "Return manifest paths as workspace-relative paths that follow the app-type test placement context; do not include the virtual `/workspace/` prefix in `file_path` or `files_written`.",
                "Every `test_id` must be globally stable and include the current node id.",
                "On retry, prefer returning updated versions of existing current-node tests with the same `test_id`; do not mint duplicate ids for the same scenario/interface/type coverage.",
                "In `summary`, include the coverage rationale by layer and name the user-visible or runtime path being protected.",
            ],
        )
    )
    return task_context_block(
        node_id=node_id,
        dynamic_context=dynamic_context,
        requirement_data=requirement_data,
        extra_sections=sections,
    )

def get_user_prompt(
    *,
    node_id: str,
    dynamic_context: str,
    interface_contract: str = "",
    test_files: list[str],
    test_type: str,
    node_tests: list[dict],
    previous_failure_summary: str = "",
) -> str:
    ordered_layers: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for layer in ("Unit", "Integration", "E2E"):
        files = [
            str(item.get("file_path", "") or "").strip()
            for item in node_tests
            if str(item.get("type", "") or "").strip().lower() == layer.lower()
            and str(item.get("file_path", "") or "").strip()
        ]
        if files:
            ordered_layers.append({"type": layer, "files": files})
    sections = [
        f"### Current Node\n`{node_id}`",
    ]
    if interface_contract.strip():
        sections.append(f"### Current Interface Contract\n{interface_contract.strip()}")
    sections.extend([
        "### Dynamic Context",

"""Generate the requirement-to-artifact traceability record."""

from __future__ import annotations

from synth.appspec import AppSpec


def render_traceability(spec: AppSpec) -> str:
    lines: list[str] = []
    lines.append("# Requirement traceability")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"Source specification: `{spec.source}`")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"Application family: `{spec.domain}` (capability pack `{spec.pack}`).")
    lines.append("")

    lines.append("## Atomic requirements")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("| Requirement | Section | Scenarios | Features |")
    lines.append("| --- | --- | ---: | --- |")
    for row in spec.requirements:
        features = ", ".join(f"`{feature}`" for feature in row.features) or "—"
        lines.append(f"| `{row.id}` {row.name} | {row.breadcrumb} | {row.scenarios} | {features} |")
    lines.append("")

    lines.append("## Observable vocabulary bound from the document")
    lines.append("")
    if spec.catalog:
        lines.append("| Key | Required wording |")
        lines.append("| --- | --- |")
        for key, value in sorted(spec.catalog.items()):
            lines.append(f"| `{key}` | {value} |")
    else:
        lines.append("No UI vocabulary map is registered for this capability pack.")
    lines.append("")

    lines.append("## Literals rewritten in the capability sources")
    lines.append("")
    if spec.substitutions:
        lines.append("| Capability literal | Document wording |")
        lines.append("| --- | --- |")
        for literal, value in sorted(spec.substitutions.items()):
            lines.append(f"| `{literal}` | {value} |")
    else:
        lines.append("The document uses the capability pack's own wording throughout.")
    lines.append("")

    seed = spec.seed or {}
    if spec.pack == "spreadsheet":
        lines.append("## Seeded fixture")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"- Workbook `{seed.get('workbook')}`, worksheets {seed.get('sheets')}")
        cells = seed.get("cells") or {}
        for name, value in cells.items():
            lines.append(f"- `{name}` = `{value}`")
        lines.append("")
        for item in seed.get("rejected_fixtures") or []:
            lines.append(
                f"- **Not seeded** ({item.get('scenarios')} scenarios, "
                f"{', '.join(item.get('requirements') or []) or 'unmapped'}): {item.get('given')}"
            )
        lines.append("")

    if spec.warnings:
        lines.append("## Warnings")
        lines.append("")
        for warning in spec.warnings:
            lines.append(f"- {warning}")
        lines.append("")

    return "\n".join(lines).rstrip() + "\n"

"""CLI-facing entry point for requirement-driven synthesis.

``arc_main.py`` calls :func:`run_synthesis` after the requirements path has been
resolved and before the ARC workflow manager is constructed. A document the
capability library understands is compiled into ``--output-dir`` and the CLI
returns; anything else returns ``None`` so the normal multi-agent pipeline (or,
when no model is configured, the generic pack) handles it.

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from synth.version import AGENT_BUILD, ARC_VERSION

ENV_DISABLE = "ARC_SYNTH_DISABLE"

RUNTIME_SEQUENCE = (
    "npm --prefix backend install",
    "npm --prefix frontend install",
    "npm --prefix frontend run build",
    "npm --prefix backend run db:prepare:e2e",
    "npm --prefix backend run start",
)


def synthesis_enabled() -> bool:
    value = os.environ.get(ENV_DISABLE, "").strip().lower()
    return value not in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}


def _prune_empty_dirs(root: Path) -> None:
    """Remove empty directories under ``root``, deepest first.

    ``init_debug_logger`` may have created workspace scaffolding before the
    synthesiser ran; an emitted workspace is the application alone, so anything
    left empty is dropped.
    """
    if not root.is_dir():
        return
    for path in sorted(root.rglob("*"), key=lambda item: len(item.parts), reverse=True):
        if not path.is_dir():
            continue
        try:
            next(path.iterdir())
        except StopIteration:
            path.rmdir()
        except OSError:
            continue


def _print_report(result: dict) -> None:
    output_dir = Path(result["output_dir"])
    manifest = result.get("manifest") or {}
    substitutions = result.get("substitutions") or {}
    print("")
    print("=" * 72)
    print(f"Compiled application: {result['title']}")
    print(f"agent build {AGENT_BUILD} (ARC {ARC_VERSION})")
    print("=" * 72)
    print(f"  domain          : {result['domain']} (capability pack '{result['pack']}')")
    print(f"  requirement set : {manifest.get('requirement_source', '')}")
    print(f"  atomic reqs     : {manifest.get('atomic_requirements', 0)}  scenarios: {manifest.get('scenarios', 0)}")
    print(f"  output directory: {output_dir}")
    print(f"  files written   : {result['file_count']}")
    print(
        f"  bound literals  : {substitutions.get('occurrences', 0)} rewrites in "
        f"{substitutions.get('files_changed', 0)} file(s)"
    )
    print("  application type: web")
    print("  dependencies    : express, cors, body-parser (frontend: react, vite)")
    print("  runtime sequence:")
    for command in RUNTIME_SEQUENCE:
        print(f"    $ {command}")
    print("  run             : npm --prefix backend run start")
    print("  port            : PORT (default 3000)")
    print("  verify          : node tests/smoke.js")
    generated = result.get("generated") or []
    if generated:
        print("  generated       :")
        for name in generated:
            print(f"    - {name}")
    print("")
    print("  top-level entries:")
    for entry in sorted({item.name for item in output_dir.iterdir()}):
        print(f"    - {entry}")
    warnings = result.get("warnings") or []
    if warnings:
        print("")
        print(f"  warnings ({len(warnings)}):")
        for warning in warnings[:10]:

def run_synthesis(
    requirement_path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    output_dir: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    clean: bool = True,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> int | None:
    """Compile ``requirement_path`` into ``output_dir``.

    Returns ``0`` when an application was emitted, or ``None`` when the caller
    should continue into the ARC pipeline.

    if not synthesis_enabled():
        print(f"[synth] disabled via {ENV_DISABLE}; using the ARC pipeline")
        return None

    from synth.emit import emit_application
    from synth.spec_builder import build_app_spec

    try:
        spec = build_app_spec(requirement_path)
    except Exception as exc:  # never let synthesis break the agent
        print(f"[synth] could not read the specification ({exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}); using the ARC pipeline")
        return None

    if spec is None:
        print("[synth] the specification could not be parsed; using the ARC pipeline")
        return None

    if spec.pack == "generic":
        print("[synth] no capability pack matches this specification; handing over to the ARC pipeline")
        return None

    if verbose:
        print(f"[synth] reading {spec.source}")
        print("\n".join(spec.summary_lines()))

    try:
        result = emit_application(spec, Path(output_dir), clean=clean, verbose=verbose)
    except Exception as exc:  # never let synthesis break the agent
        print(f"[synth] emission failed ({exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}); using the ARC pipeline")
        return None

    _prune_empty_dirs(Path(result["output_dir"]))
    _print_report(result)
    return 0

"""Turn a parsed requirement set into an :class:`~synth.appspec.AppSpec`."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path

from synth.appspec import AppSpec, RequirementRow
from synth.library import pack_exists
from synth.reqs import catalog
from synth.reqs.catalog import extract_catalog, load_string_map
from synth.reqs.domain import classify
from synth.reqs.fixtures import compose_sheet_seed
from synth.reqs.loader import RequirementError, load_requirement_set
from synth.reqs.model import ReqNode, RequirementSet
from synth.seed.collab import compose_collab_seed
from synth.seed.generic import compose_generic_seed


def _named_controls(text: str, *, kinds: tuple[str, ...] = ("double", "single")) -> list[str]:
    from synth.reqs.quotes import quoted_spans

    names: list[str] = []
    for span in quoted_spans(text, kinds=kinds):
        value = span.value
        if 1 <= len(value) <= 60 and value not in names:
            names.append(value)
    return names


def _feature_map(requirement_set: RequirementSet, features: list[str], matched: dict[str, list[str]], node: ReqNode) -> list[str]:
    """Which detected features this atomic requirement is responsible for."""
    own = f"{node.name} {node.description}".lower()
    assigned: list[str] = []
    for feature in features:
        terms = matched.get(feature, [])
        if any(term in own for term in terms):
            assigned.append(feature)
    return assigned


def _requirements(requirement_set: RequirementSet, features: list[str], matched: dict[str, list[str]]) -> list[RequirementRow]:
    rows: list[RequirementRow] = []
    for node in requirement_set.atomics:
        text = " ".join(
            [node.name, node.description]
            + [scenario.name for scenario in node.scenarios]
            + [step.text for scenario in node.scenarios for step in scenario.steps]
        )
        rows.append(
            RequirementRow(
                id=node.id,
                name=node.name,
                breadcrumb=node.breadcrumb,
                features=_feature_map(requirement_set, features, matched, node),
                scenarios=len(node.scenarios),
                named_controls=_named_controls(text)[:16],
            )
        )
    return rows


PACK_FAMILIES = {
    "spreadsheet": "a spreadsheet / workbook workspace: worksheets, cells, ranges, formulas, CSV import and export, sorting, filtering, pivot summaries, formatting",
    "collab": "a source-hosting and collaboration platform: accounts, sessions, organizations, repositories, branches, commits, issues, pull requests, reviews, teams, permissions",
    "collab_stage1": "the identity and organization subset of a collaboration platform: registration, sign-in, password recovery and change, sign out, organization browsing and creation, teams, membership, repository access grants — with no repositories, commits, issues or pull requests",
}


def _with_llm_family(requirement_path, requirement_set, decision, warnings: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """Ask the model to name the family when the keyword scorer cannot."""
    from synth import llm

    if not llm.enabled():
        return None
    usage = llm.Usage()
    families = {name: PACK_FAMILIES[name] for name in PACK_FAMILIES if pack_exists(name)}
    guess = llm.classify_pack(catalog.document_text(requirement_set), families, usage=usage)
    if guess:
        warnings.append(
            f"the requirement document was unclear to the local classifier ({decision.pack!r}); "
            f"the model identified capability pack {guess!r}"
        )
    return guess


def _with_llm_bindings(
    requirement_set,
    entries: list,
    result,
    warnings: list[str],
) -> None:
    """Let the model propose bindings for the literals the anchors missed."""
    from synth import llm

    if not llm.enabled():
        return
    missed = catalog.unbound_literals(result, entries)
    if not missed:
        return
    usage = llm.Usage()
    proposals = llm.propose_bindings(
        catalog.document_text(requirement_set),
        missed,
        catalog.requirement_ids(requirement_set),
        usage=usage,
    )
    if not proposals:
        return
    values, substitutions, accepted, rejected = catalog.validate_proposals(requirement_set, proposals)
    if not accepted:
        return
    result.values.update(values)
    result.substitutions.update(substitutions)
    warnings.append(
        f"the local anchors did not locate {len(missed)} capability string(s); the model proposed "
        f"{len(proposals)} binding(s), of which {len(accepted)} reproduced the pack's literal exactly"
        + (f" and {len(rejected)} did not" if rejected else "")
    )


def build_app_spec(requirement_path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> AppSpec | None:
    """Parse, classify and lift ``requirement_path`` into an :class:`AppSpec`."""
    try:
        requirement_set = load_requirement_set(requirement_path)
    except RequirementError:
        return None

    warnings: list[str] = []
    decision = classify(requirement_set)
    decision_pack = decision.pack if decision.pack in PACK_FAMILIES and pack_exists(decision.pack) else "generic"
    if decision_pack == "generic":
        guessed = _with_llm_family(requirement_path, requirement_set, decision, warnings)
        if guessed and pack_exists(guessed):
            decision_pack = guessed

    diagnostics_extra: dict = {}
    if decision_pack == "spreadsheet":
        seed = compose_sheet_seed(requirement_set).to_dict()
        # A rejected family is a recorded structural fact about the document,
        # not a defect: the families contradict each other, so no single seed
        # can satisfy them all. It is reported, not warned about.
        diagnostics_extra["rejected_fixtures"] = seed.get("rejected_fixtures", [])
    elif decision_pack in {"collab", "collab_stage1"}:
        seed = compose_collab_seed(requirement_set, pack=decision_pack)
    else:
        seed = compose_generic_seed(requirement_set)

    entries = load_string_map(decision_pack)
    catalog_result = extract_catalog(requirement_set, entries)
    if decision_pack != "generic":
        _with_llm_bindings(requirement_set, entries, catalog_result, warnings)
    warnings.extend(catalog_result.warnings)

    spec = AppSpec(
        domain=decision.domain,
        pack=decision_pack,
        title=requirement_set.title,
        source=str(Path(requirement_set.source).resolve()),
        features=list(decision.features),
        seed=seed,
        catalog=catalog_result.values,
        substitutions=catalog_result.substitutions,
        requirements=_requirements(requirement_set, decision.features, decision.matched_terms),
        diagnostics={
            "domain_scores": decision.scores,
            "matched_terms": {key: list(value) for key, value in decision.matched_terms.items()},
            "catalog_fallbacks": catalog_result.fallbacks,
            **diagnostics_extra,
        },
        warnings=warnings,
    )
    return spec

"""Ship a smoke suite with every emitted application.

A capability pack already carries the application's own suites; this module only
supplies one when a pack has none, so every emitted workspace can be verified
with the same command:

    node tests/smoke.js http://127.0.0.1:3000
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from synth.appspec import AppSpec
from synth.emit.seedjs import js


def _render_smoke(spec: AppSpec) -> str:
    seed = spec.seed or {}
    workbook = seed.get("workbook")
    sheets = list(seed.get("sheets") or [])
    cells: dict[str, str] = dict(seed.get("cells") or {})

    expectations = {
        "workbook": workbook,
        "sheets": sheets,
        "cells": cells,
    }

    return "\n".join(
        [
            "'use strict';",
            "",
            "/**",
            " * HTTP smoke checks for the generated application.",
            " *",
            " * Run against a started backend:",
            " *   node tests/smoke.js http://127.0.0.1:3000",
            " */",
            "",
            "const base = (process.argv[2] || process.env.BASE_URL || 'http://127.0.0.1:3000').replace(/\\/$/, '');",
            f"const EXPECTED = {_js_object(expectations)};",
            "",
            "let passed = 0;",
            "const failures = [];",
            "",
            "function check(name, condition, detail) {",
            "  if (condition) {",
            "    passed += 1;",
            "    return;",
            "  }",
            "  failures.push(`${name}${detail ? `: ${detail}` : ''}`);",
            "}",
            "",
            "async function get(path) {",
            "  const response = await fetch(base + path);",
            "  const text = await response.text();",
            "  let body = null;",
            "  try {",
            "    body = JSON.parse(text);",
            "  } catch {",
            "    body = text;",
            "  }",
            "  return { status: response.status, body };",
            "}",
            "",
            "async function main() {",
            "  const health = await get('/api/health');",
            "  check('health status', health.status === 200, `got ${health.status}`);",
            "  check('health payload', health.body && health.body.code === 200, JSON.stringify(health.body));",
            "",
            "  const listed = await get('/api/workbooks');",
            "  if (listed.status === 200 && Array.isArray(listed.body)) {",
            "    const names = listed.body.map((row) => row && (row.name || row.title));",
            "    check('seeded workbook is listed', names.includes(EXPECTED.workbook), names.join(', '));",
            "    const record = listed.body.find((row) => row && (row.name || row.title) === EXPECTED.workbook);",
            "    if (record) {",
            "      const opened = await get(`/api/workbooks/${record.id || record.public_id || record.publicId}`);",
            "      check('seeded workbook opens', opened.status === 200, `got ${opened.status}`);",
            "      const workbook = (opened.body && (opened.body.data || opened.body)) || {};",
            "      const sheetNames = (workbook.sheets || []).map((sheet) => sheet.name);",
            "      for (const name of EXPECTED.sheets) {",
            "        check(`worksheet ${name} exists`, sheetNames.includes(name), sheetNames.join(', '));",
            "      }",
            "      const first = (workbook.sheets || [])[0] || {};",
            "      for (const [cell, value] of Object.entries(EXPECTED.cells)) {",
            "        check(`cell ${cell}`, String((first.cells || {})[cell]) === String(value), String((first.cells || {})[cell]));",
            "      }",

            "    console.error(`${failures.length} smoke check(s) failed`);",
            "    for (const failure of failures) console.error(`  - ${failure}`);",
            "    process.exit(1);",
            "  }",
            "  console.log(`All ${passed} smoke checks passed`);",
            "}",
            "",
            "main().catch((error) => {",
            "  console.error(error);",
            "  process.exit(1);",
            "});",

        ]
    )


def _js_object(value) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        inner = ", ".join(f"{js(str(key))}: {_js_object(item)}" for key, item in value.items())
        return "{ " + inner + " }"
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return "[" + ", ".join(_js_object(item) for item in value) + "]"
    if value is None:
        return "null"
    return js(str(value))


def render_tests(spec: AppSpec, output_dir: Path) -> list[str]:
    tests_dir = output_dir / "tests"
    if tests_dir.is_dir() and any(tests_dir.iterdir()):
        return []
    tests_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (tests_dir / "smoke.js").write_text(_render_smoke(spec), encoding="utf-8")
    return ["tests/smoke.js"]

"""Decide which capability pack an application belongs to.

The decision is made from the requirement prose, never from an identifier: a
document is compared against the vocabulary of each pack, and the pack whose
vocabulary the atomic requirements actually speak wins. Nothing here depends on
a requirement *identifier* being spelled a particular way, so a document whose
``REQ-*`` labels have been rewritten still classifies the same way.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

from synth.reqs.model import RequirementSet
from synth.reqs.quotes import normalise, squeeze

#: Vocabulary that indicates each domain. Terms are matched on word boundaries
#: against the concatenated atomic requirement prose.
SPREADSHEET_TERMS = (
    "spreadsheet",
    "workbook",
    "worksheet",
    "formula",
    "cell",
    "grid",
    "pivot",
    "csv",
    "sort",
    "filter",
    "validation",
    "row",
    "column",
)

COLLAB_TERMS = (
    "repository",
    "issue",
    "pull request",
    "branch",
    "commit",
    "organization",
    "team",
    "milestone",
    "label",
    "fork",
    "account",
    "password",
    "sign in",
    "sign up",
    "profile",
    "notebook",
)

#: Feature families and the vocabulary that marks them present. Used both to
#: classify and to report what the emitter must cover.
FEATURE_TERMS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
    "auth.register": ("register a new", "create account", "create an account", "sign up", "registration"),
    "auth.signin": ("sign in", "sign-in", "log in", "login"),
    "auth.password_reset": ("forgot password", "reset password", "recovery code"),
    "auth.session": ("sign out", "sign-out", "account menu", "session"),
    "org.lifecycle": ("organization", "organisation"),
    "org.members": ("member", "people", "invite", "role"),
    "org.teams": ("team",),
    "repo.lifecycle": ("create a repository", "new repository", "repository visibility", "delete a repository"),
    "repo.files": ("file", "directory", "editor", "blob"),
    "repo.branches": ("branch",),
    "repo.commits": ("commit", "history", "diff"),
    "repo.issues": ("issue",),
    "repo.pulls": ("pull request",),
    "repo.milestones": ("milestone",),
    "repo.labels": ("label",),
    "repo.fork": ("fork",),
    "repo.search": ("search",),
    "sheet.workbook_lifecycle": ("create a blank workbook", "rename a workbook", "blank workbook"),
    "sheet.workbook_navigation": ("view and open", "workbook home", "open a workbook"),
    "sheet.csv": ("csv",),
    "sheet.worksheet_lifecycle": ("add a worksheet", "switch worksheet", "rename a worksheet", "delete a worksheet"),
    "sheet.structure": ("insert and delete rows", "insert and delete columns", "row and column structure"),
    "sheet.entry": ("edit a cell", "direct data entry", "formula bar"),
    "sheet.range_transfer": ("copy, cut", "undo and redo", "rectangular cell range"),
    "sheet.formula": ("formula", "recalculate", "aggregate"),
    "sheet.formula_errors": ("formula error", "display and fix"),
    "sheet.sort": ("sort",),
    "sheet.filter": ("filter",),
    "sheet.validation": ("data validation", "dropdown or numeric"),
    "sheet.pivot": ("pivot",),
}

_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9' ]+")


@dataclass(slots=True)
class DomainDecision:
    domain: str
    pack: str
    scores: dict[str, int]
    features: list[str]
    matched_terms: dict[str, list[str]]

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "domain": self.domain,
            "pack": self.pack,
            "scores": self.scores,
            "features": list(self.features),
            "matched_terms": {key: list(value) for key, value in self.matched_terms.items()},
        }


def _haystack(requirement_set: RequirementSet) -> str:
    chunks: list[str] = []
    for node in requirement_set.atomics:
        chunks.append(squeeze(normalise(node.name)))
        chunks.append(squeeze(normalise(node.description)))
        for scenario in node.scenarios:
            chunks.append(squeeze(normalise(scenario.name)))
            for step in scenario.steps:
                chunks.append(step.text)
    return " ".join(chunks).lower()


def _count_terms(haystack: str, terms: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
    hits: list[str] = []
    score = 0
    for term in terms:
        if " " in term or "-" in term or "'" in term:
            found = haystack.count(term)
        else:
            found = len(re.findall(rf"\b{re.escape(term)}\b", haystack))
        if found:
            hits.append(term)
            score += found
    return score, hits


def detect_features(requirement_set: RequirementSet) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, list[str]]]:
    """Feature ids implied by the document, plus the terms that implied them."""
    haystack = _haystack(requirement_set)
    features: list[str] = []
    matched: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for feature, terms in FEATURE_TERMS.items():
        score, hits = _count_terms(haystack, terms)
        if score:
            features.append(feature)
            matched[feature] = hits
    return features, matched


def classify(requirement_set: RequirementSet) -> DomainDecision:
    haystack = _haystack(requirement_set)
    features, matched = detect_features(requirement_set)

    sheet_score, sheet_hits = _count_terms(haystack, SPREADSHEET_TERMS)
    collab_score, collab_hits = _count_terms(haystack, COLLAB_TERMS)

    # Requirement identifiers are numbered REQ-<chapter>-…; the spreadsheet
    # document spreads its chapters over workbook, worksheet, cell, formula and
    # analysis work, so the raw term counts separate the two domains by a wide
    # margin. Ties and unrecognised documents fall back to the generic pack.
    if sheet_score == 0 and collab_score == 0:
        domain = "generic"
    elif sheet_score >= collab_score * 1.2:
        domain = "spreadsheet"
    else:
        domain = "collab"

    if domain == "collab":
        # The stage-1 document covers accounts and organizations only. It has no
        # issue, pull-request, branch or commit family at all, which is exactly
        # what distinguishes it from the full collaboration platform.
        deep_families = {"repo.pulls", "repo.issues", "repo.commits", "repo.branches", "repo.milestones", "repo.labels", "repo.fork"}
        domain = "collab" if deep_families & set(features) else "collab-stage1"

    pack = {"spreadsheet": "spreadsheet", "collab": "collab", "collab-stage1": "collab_stage1", "generic": "generic"}[domain]

    return DomainDecision(
        domain=domain,
        pack=pack,
        scores={"spreadsheet": sheet_score, "collab": collab_score},
        features=features,
        matched_terms={"spreadsheet": sheet_hits, "collab": collab_hits, **matched},
    )

"""Bind an :class:`~synth.appspec.AppSpec` into a capability library tree.

The emitter is deliberately literal about what it does:

1. copy the capability pack for the inferred domain into the output directory;
2. rewrite every registered library literal to the wording the document uses;
3. replace the modules the pack marks as *generated* (the spreadsheet seed, the
   shipped test suite, the README) with files built from the AppSpec;
4. write ``.arc/spec.json`` and ``.arc/traceability.md`` so a reader can see
   which requirement produced which file.

Nothing in step 1 depends on the document, so an emitted application is
"roughly the same content" as the template by construction; steps 2 and 3 are
what make it a function of the document rather than a copy of the template.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

from synth.appspec import AppSpec
from synth.emit.readme import render_readme
from synth.emit.seedjs import render_seed_modules, seed_coverage
from synth.emit.substitute import build_substitutions, substitute_tree
from synth.emit.tests import render_tests
from synth.emit.trace import render_traceability
from synth.library import library_path, pack_exists

SPEC_JSON = ".arc/spec.json"
TRACEABILITY = ".arc/traceability.md"
BUILD_MANIFEST = ".arc/build.json"
SKIP_NAMES = {"MANIFEST.json"}


def _copy_pack(pack: str, output_dir: Path, *, clean: bool) -> int:
    source = library_path(pack)
    if clean and output_dir.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(output_dir)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    copied = 0
    for path in sorted(source.rglob("*")):
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        if path.name in SKIP_NAMES:
            continue
        relative = path.relative_to(source)
        destination = output_dir / relative
        destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(path, destination)
        copied += 1
    return copied


def _count_files(root: Path) -> int:
    return sum(1 for path in root.rglob("*") if path.is_file())


def emit_application(
    spec: AppSpec,
    output_dir: Path,
    *,
    clean: bool = True,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> dict:
    if not pack_exists(spec.pack):
        raise RuntimeError(f"capability pack not built: {spec.pack} (run tools/build_library.py)")

    output_dir = output_dir.resolve()
    started = time.time()
    copied = _copy_pack(spec.pack, output_dir, clean=clean)

    substitutions = build_substitutions(spec)
    stats = substitute_tree(output_dir, substitutions)

    generated = render_seed_modules(spec, output_dir)
    generated.extend(render_tests(spec, output_dir))
    readme = render_readme(spec)
    (output_dir / "README.md").write_text(readme, encoding="utf-8")
    generated.append("README.md")

    (output_dir / ".arc").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    spec.write(output_dir / SPEC_JSON)
    (output_dir / TRACEABILITY).write_text(render_traceability(spec), encoding="utf-8")

    coverage = seed_coverage(spec, output_dir)
    missing = {kind: values for kind, values in coverage["missing"].items() if values}

    from synth.emit.selfcheck import check_seed, check_tree

    selfcheck = check_tree(output_dir) + check_seed(spec, output_dir)
    if selfcheck:
        raise RuntimeError("the emitted application does not satisfy the runtime contract: " + "; ".join(selfcheck))

    manifest = {
        "generator": "arc-synthesis",
        "generated_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "domain": spec.domain,
        "pack": spec.pack,
        "requirement_source": spec.source,
        "requirement_set_title": spec.title,
        "atomic_requirements": len(spec.requirements),
        "scenarios": sum(row.scenarios for row in spec.requirements),
        "copied_from_library": copied,
        "generated_files": sorted(generated),
        "literal_substitutions": stats.as_dict(),
        "seed_coverage": coverage,
        "warnings": list(spec.warnings),
        "elapsed_seconds": round(time.time() - started, 3),
    }
    (output_dir / BUILD_MANIFEST).write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    result = {
        "domain": spec.domain,
        "pack": spec.pack,
        "title": spec.title,
        "output_dir": str(output_dir),
        "file_count": _count_files(output_dir),
        "generated": sorted(generated),
        "substitutions": stats.as_dict(),
        "seed_coverage": coverage,
        "warnings": list(spec.warnings),
        "manifest": manifest,
    }

    if verbose:
        print(f"[synth] capability pack '{spec.pack}': {copied} files copied, {len(generated)} generated")
        print(
            f"[synth] rewrote {stats.total} literal occurrence(s) across "
            f"{stats.files_changed} file(s) from {len(substitutions)} document-stated literal(s)"
        )
        if missing:
            total_missing = sum(len(values) for values in missing.values())
            print(f"[synth] {total_missing} declared seed value(s) are not materialised by this capability pack:")
            for kind, values in list(missing.items())[:8]:
                preview = ", ".join(str(value) for value in values[:6])
                print(f"[synth]   {kind}: {preview}")
        for warning in spec.warnings[:8]:
            print(f"[synth] warning: {warning}")
        print(f"[synth] wrote {result['file_count']} files to {output_dir}")
    return result
